sections.h2: Ways to sell a house in Stonecrest
sections.html:
Homeowners here usually pick from three paths: hire a listing agent, go it alone, or take a cash offer from an investor who handles repairs. Pick based on how much work the house needs, your payoff balance, your move-out date, and whether a tenant or relative is still inside.

  • Agents suit houses that show well and owners who can wait for the right buyer.
  • Selling on your own saves the commission, but price, disclosures and negotiation are all yours.
  • Cash offers are worth collecting when the house has deferred repairs, back taxes or an estate attached to it.

Stonecrest sits inside DeKalb County, so county offices handle property tax on every parcel, while the city keeps its own permit and business license staff. Knowing which office answers which question saves a lot of phone calls once you have a buyer.

The city is young. Incorporation passed by vote on November 8, 2016, and the city began operating on July 10, 2017. Its own staff cover zoning, code enforcement, business licenses and building permits. The county still provides police, fire, road upkeep and sanitation. The city set its first millage rate in 2020, so ask the DeKalb Tax Commissioner what city levy, if any, appears on your bill.

The estimated population is 61,337, in 20,995 households, and owners occupy 56.3 percent of the homes. That mix of owners and renters means investors who plan to rent the house out are a real part of the buyer pool.

sections.h2: What buyers like about the area
sections.html:
Retail in the city centers on the Mall at Stonecrest, ringed by medical, office and hotel parcels around it and DeKalb Medical Center at Hillandale as the main hospital. Interstate 20 and State Routes 124 and 278 lead toward downtown Atlanta and Hartsfield-Jackson airport. Two industrial areas hold some of the larger local employers, so a buyer who works at one of them may want a short drive.

Outdoor space is the other draw. The Arabia Mountain National Heritage Area covers 2,550 acres of exposed granite, wetlands, streams, lakes and forest linked by trails, and Davidson-Arabia Mountain Nature Park and Panola Mountain State Park sit nearby. A listing or a cash pitch can mention the drive to the mall corridor or the trailheads, since those are the things people ask about first.

sections.h2: DeKalb property tax due dates and penalties
sections.html:
Bills go out in August addressed to whoever held title on January 1, and the county sends another to the current owner if that is a different person. Choose between two payments (September 30 and November 15) or one payment by September 30. If you mail a check, the envelope needs a hand-canceled postmark from the post office on or before the date. A meter stamp or kiosk label will not count. Anything late carries a 5 percent penalty.

The county does not mail bills to lenders. If your mortgage payment includes escrow, confirm with your servicer that the tax was actually sent before you list.

On a single-family home, the county prints a yearly sanitation assessment for trash pickup of $362.30 on the same bill.

When a sale closes after January 1, the county tells the new owner to check the closing statement or ask the closing attorney, lender or escrow agent who is responsible. Whatever is unpaid stays attached to the parcel. Have the attorney itemize the tax line on the settlement statement so both sides see the split.

If the taxes are overdue when you sell, the payoff comes out of your proceeds at the table. A cash buyer usually accepts that arrangement without a problem, which is one reason owners with back taxes ask for cash bids.

sections.h2: Homestead exemption and appeals in DeKalb
sections.html:
To qualify for the DeKalb homestead exemption you must occupy the house as your primary home on January 1, hold a Georgia license or ID showing the address, and register your vehicles there. Filing closes in mid-July. Exemptions are never automatic and never pass to a buyer, so the new owner has to apply on their own. Once granted, an exemption puts an assessment freeze on county taxes that may limit increases, though it does not touch school, city or state taxes.

  • Special exemptions with income limits exist for homeowners 62 and older, disabled homeowners, former service members rated 100 percent disabled, and some surviving spouses.
  • The appeal clock is 45 days from the notice. Fax and email filings get rejected, so deliver it by hand or mail.
  • Your forum choices are the Board of Equalization (free), nonbinding arbitration ($217 plus a certified appraisal), or a hearing officer, which is open only to non-homestead property valued over $500,000.
  • An appeal still open when bills print means you pay on a temporary value, typically the lower of last year's final figure or 85 percent of this year's.

Property is appraised at 100 percent of fair market value and assessed at 40 percent. The Property Appraisal Department is at 325 Swanton Way in Decatur, and the Tax Commissioner's central office is at 4380 Memorial Drive in Decatur.

A deed cannot be recorded in Georgia until transfer tax has been paid. The seller is the responsible party by default, though the sales contract can say otherwise. The state Department of Revenue posts the rate on its transfer tax page, and the PT-61 declaration is filed online by you or the closing office.

Not sure your transfer is taxable? Call the county's Clerk of Superior Court. In an ordinary sale the closing attorney files the form and deducts the tax from your proceeds.

sections.h2: Checklist before you accept an offer
sections.html:
1. Pull together your deed, DeKalb parcel number and latest assessment notice.
  2. Look up whether you have a homestead exemption on file, and let buyers know it ends with your ownership.
  3. Open the August bill and mark which installments you have paid.
  4. Ask your servicer for a payoff figure and the closing attorney for a lien search.
  5. Weigh each offer by the net you walk away with after transfer tax, repair credits and the closing date.

A cash sale skips the buyer's loan approval and appraisal, which removes two common ways a deal stalls. The price is often lower in exchange, so keep two or three bids in front of you.

faqs.a: Yes. Voters created it on November 8, 2016, and it began operating on July 10, 2017. The city runs zoning, permits and business licenses, while DeKalb County bills property tax and handles public safety.

faqs.q: When are DeKalb County property tax installments due?
faqs.a: Installments fall on September 30 and November 15, and paying everything at once means doing it by September 30. Late payments draw a 5 percent penalty under strict postmark rules.

faqs.q: Does my DeKalb homestead exemption go to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. Exemptions cannot be transferred, so a buyer applies separately and must meet the January 1 ownership and residency tests.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my DeKalb property value?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the mailing date on the assessment notice. Deliver the appeal by hand or have it postmarked by then, because fax and email filings are refused.

faqs.q: Who is responsible for the property tax bill after I sell in Stonecrest?
faqs.a: The closing statement settles it. DeKalb mails a bill to the January 1 owner and to the new owner, and buyers are told to ask the closing attorney or escrow agent who owes it. Unpaid tax stays with the property.
